subject: science

entries: Inside the atom - shells draw themselves around a tiny dense nucleus that grows at the centre, electrons drop into shell 1, and the space between stays empty: the atom is mostly empty space.
slots.label: Inside the atom
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Counting particles: carbon - carbon is element 6, so six protons in the nucleus and six electrons around it fill the shells two, then four: 2,4.
slots.label: Carbon
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Counting particles: sodium - sodium is element 11 with eleven protons, twelve neutrons and eleven electrons arranged 2,8,1, and the lone outer electron rules its chemistry.
slots.label: Sodium
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Groups: the table's columns - a group shares the same number of outer electrons down the column, so its elements react in similar ways.
slots.label: Groups
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Periods: the table's rows - the period number matches the number of electron shells: period 2 has two shells, period 3 has three.
slots.label: Periods
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake - the ball-and-stick model makes atoms look like solid marbles, but the nucleus is a speck in the middle of empty space and electrons sit in fixed shells.
slots.label: Common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The smallest particle of an element that keeps its chemical identity: a tiny dense nucleus with electrons in shells around mostly empty space.
slots.label: Atom
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The tiny dense centre of the atom, holding the protons and neutrons. Almost all the atom's mass sits here.
slots.label: Nucleus
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A particle in the nucleus with charge +1 and mass 1. The number of protons - the proton number - fixes which element the atom is.
slots.label: Proton
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A particle in the nucleus with no charge and mass 1. Neutrons = nucleon number - proton number.
slots.label: Neutron
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A particle with charge -1 and almost no mass, sitting in fixed shells around the nucleus. A neutral atom has equal electrons and protons.
slots.label: Electron
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A fixed energy level around the nucleus where electrons sit. Shells fill in order: shell 1 holds 2, shell 2 holds 8, shell 3 holds 8.
slots.label: Electron shell
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A column of the periodic table. Elements in one group share the same number of outer electrons, so they react in similar ways.
slots.label: Group
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A row of the periodic table. The period number matches the number of electron shells the atoms have.
slots.label: Period
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: Atomic structure and the periodic table
